messages:
deploybot: Release pointer 'release-hotfix-2026-03-20' created from commit abc1234 (merge PR #789). Short changelog: fixed KV cache eviction causing OOM under heavy batching; adjusted kernel selection heuristic for short sequences; minor observability logs. Target: canary in us-west-2. Canary start in ~10m. Note: this release updates a kernel driver and requires node pod restarts.

amanda_ux: Can we add a short customer-impact line to the changelog? Any migration steps?

marc_engineer: No data migrations. Only runtime/driver update. Plan: drain canary pods, restart, monitor KV eviction metrics. If something goes sideways, rollback to the previous release pointer.

liam_sre: @deploybot please pin prod to the current stable for the weekend and add a QA hold for 60m after canary finishes.

deploybot: Pinned prod to 'release-stable-2026-03-18'. Canary scheduled at 2189012700. QA hold set to 60 minutes after canary. Tag & commit:

```
git tag -a release-hotfix-2026-03-20 abc1234 -m "hotfix: KV cache OOM fix"
git push origin release-hotfix-2026-03-20
```

Rollback helper (ops):

```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/serving-runtime --to-revision=3
# or update pointer: deploybot update-pointer release-hotfix -> release-hotfix-previous
```

anya_qe: I'll run smoke + KV stress tests during the QA hold and post results here. Checklist: latency baseline, KV memory under load, eviction rate.

marc_engineer: FYI you can also revert the pointer via git if needed: `git push origin :release-hotfix-current` then push previous tag. Prefer deploybot pointer update for atomicity.

deploybot: Canary started. Status: 2/2 pods updated, readiness probes passing. Initial probe metrics look nominal. Monitoring for 15m and will report back. :eyes:

liam_sre: Copy. If CPU/oom spikes or error rate >1% escalate to #incidents and page oncall.
